title: Overhead clearance screening along East 7th Street, Austin, Texas, from open LiDAR

headline.label: lowest overhead clearance found along 1.4 km of East 7th Street

method: Took the OpenStreetMap centreline of East 7th Street between Congress Avenue and Chicon Street (1,406 m) and moved it into EPSG:26914, the CRS of the LiDAR.
Read only the points within 25 m of the route from the COPC files, in 100 m pieces (454,965 points).
Stations every 1 m; road surface = median height of ground and road returns within 3 m of the centreline over 5 m, interpolated where the road is hidden (97% of stations measured directly).

Overhead returns: every non-ground, non-noise point within 5 m of the centreline and 2.5 to 30 m above the road; the clearance at a station is the lowest of them, with its class as the data provider classified it.
limits: Screening, not a clearance survey or a route permit. Airborne LiDAR sees surfaces from above: for a bridge it records the top of the deck, so the true clearance under the soffit is lower by the deck depth, and thin wires and branches under a canopy can be missed. The data were flown in 2019; trees grow and are cut, and roads and bridges are rebuilt since.
